reason: This passage (Exodus 17:8-16) describes the battle with Amalek at Rephidim. The Hebrew leaders—Moses, Joshua, Aaron, and Hur—are actively engaged in military leadership and strategy. Moses directs Joshua to select men and fight Amalek, while Moses himself holds up the staff of God from a hilltop. When his hands grow weary, Aaron and Hur support them. The narrative focuses on the military victory achieved through the leaders' coordinated effort, not on any complaint by leaders about the people. The people (Israel) are portrayed as fighting effectively, particularly when Moses's hands are raised.
